prediction.likelyOutcome: A genuine toss-up on the pivotal issue: whether Paragraph 4.5's application-of-payments clause can validly convert a 2023 shortfall into 'currently due' rent for a February 2025 three-day notice under CCP §1161(2), compounded by a strong tenant-side waiver/estoppel argument from 23 months of accepted full rent. Universal is more likely than not to eventually recover the underlying $65,989 in some form (via this UD action or a follow-on contract suit), but its chances of winning the summary UD remedy itself — and therefore the holdover damages and possession relief — are close to even, with equities tilting toward the tenant.

outcome.description: After a three-day court trial the trial court entered judgment for the landlord on July 3, 2025 awarding possession, $65,989 in past-due rent (the amount demanded in the notice) and $123,111 in holdover damages, $189,100 in total; no fee award is stated in the opinion. The Court of Appeal reversed, holding the three-day notice void because the unpaid rent fell due more than one year before service, and remanded for entry of judgment in favor of the tenant.
outcome.finalNote: Reversed: the three-day notice was void, so the landlord takes nothing in this action.
